text:
tess_sales: Heads-up — Prospect Borealis wants a POC with committed capacity. They quoted a summer marketing surge: 1.8k QPS peaks, steady ~350 qps, workload is 55% chat (avg 120 tokens) + 45% embeddings. They want price predictability and KMS/audit for HIPAA. Need sizing + fallback.
raj_oncall: Do we have pinned model and preferred region? Also concurrency per session and expected session time?
amar_eng: They're pinning to redwood/llm-7b-quantized in eu-west-1. Avg session ~8 turns, median concurrency during peak spikes ~1100 concurrent. Embed dim 768.
bev_solution: Billing ask: give them a simple committed seat quote + burst pool option. They hate surprise overages. Also ask about preheat for KV so campaign doesn't start cold.
tess_sales: Exactly. Can we recommend reservation count + burst plan and a preheat addon estimate?
amar_eng: Ballpark throughput: chat at 120 tokens ~45 qps per A100-80 per GPU; embeddings ~1000 embed ops/s per GPU when batched. Mixed effective =~ 65 qps/GPU. For steady 350 -> 6 GPUs reserved. For 1800 peak -> ~28 GPUs total, so reserve 6 + burst up to 22.
raj_oncall: Operational constraints: fast scale-up is required, but KV cache warms slowly. Recommend reserve to cover steady + short buffer, autoscale for remainder. Scale-up target ~60s to add nodes, scale-down cooldown 10min.
amar_eng: Suggest also an emergency fallback routing to a smaller-precision variant (llm-7b-q4f16) if burst > threshold. Use a canary 5-10% to validate quality during the surge.
bev_solution: Can we present pricing as: monthly fee for 6 reserved GPUs, capped burst credits (e.g., up to 22 GPUs billed at burst rate), and optional preheat block of 6 GPU-hours per campaign start?
raj_oncall: Add a clause: we offer a burst soft-cap — after X hours of sustained burst we engage a mitigation plan (traffic shaping, rate limiting) to protect cluster. Need to document this for legal.
tess_sales: Customer will want SLA language around latency. Clarify that p99 targets assume reserved capacity and warming; cold cache during sudden spikes may violate p99.
amar_eng: I'll draft a short engineering appendix with ceiling latency numbers at 6, 10, 15, 28 GPUs and expected token-level cost per response. Also include preheat token estimate: if they warm common prefixes it's ~150M tokens -> ~2.5 GPU-hours per region to warm, recommend 4-6h preheat window to be safe.
raj_oncall: For HA: recommend AZ spread for reserved nodes (min 3 AZs when reserving 6 GPUs). Cross-region failover supported but doubles preheat effort and adds replication cost. Call that out.
bev_solution: For quality-sensitive customers, offer a controlled fallback policy: canary 10% to fallback during surge, escalate to 30% if eval drift < 1.5%, cap at 50% max. Make these numbers configurable in contract.
amar_eng: Example config snippet for their engineering appendix:
```
reserved:
  nodes: 6
  min: 6
  max: 28
  scale_up_policy: {qps_threshold: 420, scale_window_sec: 60}
  scale_down_policy: {qps_threshold: 280, cooldown_sec: 600}
fallbacks:
  - name: llm-7b-q4f16
    canary_percent: 10
    max_percent: 50
```
raj_oncall: Ops runbook items to include: preheat checklist, KV-hit monitoring dashboard, tail-latency alarm, automated throttling recipe, and incident contact list.
infra-bot: Created ticket #PR-9022: "Borealis POC 1: sizing appendix + preheat runbook + legal KMS wording" assigned to amar_eng, raj_oncall, due 2026-04-12. :white_check_mark:
tess_sales: Great. Bev, can you convert the engineering appendix into a pricing exhibit with three scenarios (steady, typical campaign, worst-case sustained)?
bev_solution: On it. I'll draft three line items: reserved monthly, burst credits pool, and one-time preheat block. Include example cost under a 3-day campaign.
amar_eng: One more note: recommend instrumenting prompt/eval hooks so we can detect quality regressions if fallback used. Add this to canary monitoring.
All: Thanks everyone 44d we'll sync with Borealis on Thu 10am CET.
